sculpt.reason: Named stroke regions apply the picked brush from the keyboard or pointer (typed brush + region, undoable), and Remesh really snaps the surface to 0.02 m voxels with an acknowledgement and Undo.

city.reason: A native density slider changes generation and the viewport supports keyboard orbit and zoom.

fly.reason: The native timeline seeks the rendered scene by keyboard or pointer and explicitly resumes playback.

fpv.reason: The mode switch relabels the rendered flight HUD; the camera path is a non-interactive preview.

light.reason: A named temperature slider works independently of keyboard orbit and zoom; presets can be compared without a pointer.

trigger.reason: Walk buttons move the player without a pointer; when you walk into the volume the trigger fires and emits trigger_fired with its count, and the status line reports it.

globe.reason: A roving flight list is the keyboard equivalent of picking a path (typed flight, from, to); traffic is labelled demo/synthetic and the footer handoffs name the selected flight.

gen3d.reason: Variants are labelled toggles that emit a typed select; the footer requests an export or Blender import of the chosen variant and the acknowledgement says no file has been delivered yet.

sim.reason: The run is labelled a scripted demo and can be paused; checkpoints capture step and reward, and Export requests that checkpoint as a typed export_policy without claiming a file exists.

inbox.reason: Message selection and archive have separate keyboard actions; local dismissal offers Undo.

thread.reason: The fact chip identifies a specific entity; the draft can be edited and Send offers Undo.

approve.reason: Explicit scope, duration, denial and revoke make the commit and its consequences legible.

chat.reason: A quick reply emits a send intent; custom text and unsend are available.

notify.reason: Batch dismissal has a deliberate button and Undo alongside the swipe affordance.

slots.reason: Suggest emits a separate intent; the grid can be moved and resized without a pointer.

kanban.reason: Selection now works by Enter and Space; arrow moves emit the affected issue and offer Undo.

390.control: MIR-327 Fix login loop on Safari. Arrow left or right to move.

1280.control: MIR-327 Fix login loop on Safari. Arrow left or right to move.

triage.reason: The Apply intent scopes the issue and priority, and triage can be reversed.

file.reason: The open intent points to a specific page rather than an opaque document link.

graph.reason: The selected note passes typed context and replies with its neighbors.

search.reason: Refine exposes a real filter; a chosen result hands its locator back to the agent.

feed.reason: The draft is editable before posting and local Undo allows unposting.

frames.reason: The inline note separates a change request from the held approval.

sign.reason: Decline is a separate route with reasons; the step indicator tracks progress.

context.reason: The card distinguishes retained files from reclaimed context, emits typed intent and offers Undo.

receipt.reason: Payment is held, costs are visible before commit, and scheduling is a reversible alternative.

metric.reason: The same bucket intent is reachable via a named slider and Ask button or by clicking the chart. Threshold alerts are reversible.

track.reason: Watching and stopping updates are in-place; the help path describes constraints.

crm.reason: Stage movement is visible and reversible; call notes are editable inline.

ride.reason: The request is held, the chosen tier is reflected in the result, and a timed cancellation is offered.

route.reason: Navigation acknowledges the specific first step and phone handoff is separate.

boarding.reason: Seat options disclose price and allow correction with Undo.

player.reason: A labelled seek slider provides keyboard and pointer scrubbing alongside playback.

workout.reason: Splits disclose useful detail before sharing; sharing notes route privacy.

home.reason: Presets and the labelled knob report the actual level.

merge.reason: The diff provides review context before the user resolves and advances checks.

ci.reason: A named job exposes its own evidence and rerunning is separate.

deploy.reason: Cancel is available during the build, with separate held promotion and rollback once ready.

incident.reason: Rollback is a separate held decision with explicit target, timeline and next exit criterion.

migrate.reason: Pause is scoped between batches; SQL inspection states locking and reversibility.

nodes.reason: The node passes named context to the agent; the canvas scrolls inside the card at narrow widths.

timeline.reason: Clips are a roving, focusable track: Enter or click marks a clip (typed clip + timecode) and seeks the monitor; Cut marked ripple-deletes with an agent acknowledgement and a 6 s Undo.

review.reason: The frame is focusable: arrows steer a marker and Enter drops a mark with its timecode and region, the same as drawing; Send hands the typed mark ids over, and the compare handle is a keyboard slider.

layers.reason: The user can choose a labelled variant before emitting the Keep handoff.

gallery.reason: Open and Select are separate paths, and the preview supports keyboard navigation and dismissal.

cad.reason: The draft is editable: arrows + Enter place points, Backspace/Escape undo and end, and a command line takes @dx,dy metres; a live length readout and Send draft hand the typed walls to the agent.

board.reason: The board is focusable: arrows move your cursor, Enter starts and finishes a shape with the current tool (emits draw), Text/Sticky place notes and Select picks a shape, all without a pointer.

daw.reason: Clips launch/stop with aria-pressed and a typed launch intent, Delete clears a clip with Undo; piano-roll notes are focusable (↑↓ transpose, ←→ move, Delete with Undo) and the transport plays and stops.

flash.reason: Reveal and self-rating are separate and the card shows scheduler context.

stage.reason: Keyboard or pointer can mute a named layer and reveal the next strongest opinion; variants remain selectable.

anatomy.reason: Accessible figure buttons select recorded loops and immediately update the numbered caption.

cua-action.reason: Window and element selection are typed fixture intents; a request never claims a driver has dispatched it.

work-dock.reason: The hold details disclose choices and boundaries without silently carrying them out.

cua-spaces.reason: Desktop and window targets are pressed toggles that switch the simulated display readout and emit a typed preview-display intent; the card is labelled fixture-only and claims no live Space.

screen.reason: Takeover emits an intent rather than claiming to control the display; saving the trajectory is separate.

sandbox.reason: The fork tree is real state without autoplay: forks are a radio group with their evidence, and Hold to keep returns a typed result { keep, stop[], evidence } and settles the card.

twin.reason: Deploy is a typed decision (policy, from, law, robots, target: twin) with the v3→v4 change stated up front and a Roll back to v3 that emits rollback_policy; laws are pick-to-context buttons.

ace-facility.reason: Floors and zones are selectable; a zone pick emits a typed select_zone intent and spec-vs-observed labels keep the twin honest about what is modelled.

form-check.reason: Timed corrections seek the set to their landmark frame and name the fault and cue; sending cues to a coach is a separate typed intent.

swing.reason: Phase buttons scrub the swing to each phase and update its readout; comparison is a separate typed intent.

health.reason: The rationale is callable; adding the plan is a distinct handoff. Source-specific coverage belongs to EU-017.

health-activity.reason: Source-specific synthetic payloads (Apple Health and Google Fit) with their own units and provenance; metrics and days are pressable readouts and 'Explain this number' emits a typed intent naming the source field.

health-recovery.reason: Source-specific synthetic payloads (Oura, WHOOP and NOOP) with their own units and provenance; metrics and days are pressable readouts and 'Explain this number' emits a typed intent naming the source field.

health-nutrition.reason: Source-specific synthetic payloads (MyFitnessPal and Lifesum) with their own units and provenance; metrics and days are pressable readouts and 'Explain this number' emits a typed intent naming the source field.

fleet-hosts.reason: The host snapshot opens an individual work item and keeps operator status visible.

fleet-portfolio.reason: The task intent is scoped to the chosen portfolio; selecting next is separate.

fleet-factory.reason: The factory opens the chosen node by keyboard or pointer with an explicit scope.

390.control: card picker, Live: TEK → PRIO → fresh bugs → salvage

1280.control: card picker, Live: TEK → PRIO → fresh bugs → salvage

gev-contacts.reason: Filtering is reversible and each contact discloses available or unavailable data.

intent-declare.reason: The review request is explicit and does not grant authority or execute a contract.

intent-contract.reason: Boundaries are inspectable and the card distinguishes review scope from approval.

intent-work.reason: The dependency view explicitly separates deferred work from the active slice.

intent-proof.reason: Opening a proof source preserves the difference between evidence and execution.

intel-decisions.reason: The local view can group decisions by provider without claiming it changes routing.

intel-value.reason: Coverage and denominator caveats are discoverable on the same card as the metric.

intel-context.reason: Source coverage can be expanded separately from the reported context numbers.

intel-health.reason: The operator can drill into gaps without implying a health check or a repair ran.

intel-suite.reason: The tab intent identifies the selected view while provenance remains part of the snapshot.

ops-burn.reason: The harness filter changes scope without overstating projected burn.

ops-alive.reason: The row filter distinguishes observed working sessions from inferred or idle states.

ops-incidents.reason: The filter separates observed kills from likely causes and keeps provenance visible.

ops-fleet.reason: The selected lane is handed back as an entity, without implying control over pods.

ops-slow.reason: An individual slow row can be retained with source context rather than pinning the whole card.

ops-models.reason: The harness filter narrows the model view within the snapshot.

ops-tokens.reason: The unit toggle distinguishes token counts from API-equivalent estimates.

ops-context.reason: The row-level context selection is separate from host state and keeps the source visible.

ops-tools.reason: The errors slice carries its filter context and is reversible.

ops-routing.reason: The row selection retains evidence rather than executing routing changes.

ops-sources.reason: An explicit source-gap row can be retained without inventing the missing telemetry.

plugin.reason: Inspection is separate from the held run action and exposes the specific call chain.

trace.reason: Spans are reachable without a pointer: Previous/Next span buttons and the focusable timeline (arrows, +/-, 0, Escape) select and reveal a span, open its drawer and emit a typed select (span, track, session).

trace-span.reason: The user can switch evidence kinds without interpreting an empty or stale detail pane.

trace-summary.reason: Read-only aggregate by design; the only action retains this summary as context.

trace-usage.reason: The provider grouping makes billing scope inspectable without side effects.

trace-tools.reason: Each tool row has a real button (aria-expanded) that opens its spans by keyboard or pointer and emits focus_tool; span rows are buttons that emit a typed select and open the drawer.

trace-errors.reason: Signature rows expand from a focusable button (aria-expanded, focus kept across re-render) and emit focus_error; every "Jump to span" is a button that emits a typed select.

trace-compare.reason: Both session pickers are named; Swap reverses sides and recalculates the displayed deltas.

trace-frustration.reason: The range picker scopes a clearly labelled feedback sample.

infra-architecture.reason: Selecting a service emits a typed select (node, service); the inspector names its connections, asks the agent with an inline acknowledgement, and removal is undoable.

infra-cluster.reason: Opening a workload emits a typed select (cluster, namespace, workload); each workload has an Ask agent handoff whose acknowledgement says the snapshot is authored, not live.

infra-iac.reason: The filter emits the shown change addresses, opening a change emits a typed select, and "Ask agent to review shown" hands the set over with an acknowledgement that nothing is applied.

infra-models.reason: Each stage emits a typed select (stage, runtime, step); the inspector states "Verified: nothing yet" and hands a stage check plan to the agent with an honest acknowledgement.
